<description>
When testing a hardware wallet integration, I found that when attempting to create a wallet with the wrong app open on the hardware wallet, the GUI crashes instead of showing an error message. After restarting, when attempting to create a wallet with the same name again, it fails with "Database already exists". Over RPC, there's no crash, but `createwallet` returns error code -1 and leaves the same files and directories behind.

This happens when setting up an external-signer wallet. When the signer fails, setting up the wallet throws `std::runtime_error`, and `CreateWallet()` doesn't catch it. The GUI's worker thread has no handler, so the uncaught exception ends in `std::terminate`, and RPC's catch-all turns it into error code -1. The directory and `wallet.dat` are created before setup and never removed when setup fails.

This uncaught exception has been encountered previously in bitcoin-core/gui#395, and bitcoin-core/gui#396 stopped the dialog from enabling the "External signer" option, but didn't handle the exception.

Commit 1 catches the exception as `LoadWalletInternal()` does. The GUI shows an error dialog, and RPC returns error code -4, with the message starting with "Wallet creation failed."
Commit 2 ensures that on failure, it removes only what was created. It checks what exists with `fs::symlink_status()`, as `MakeDatabase()` does, so a `wallet.dat` symlink is kept even if its target doesn't exist, and it logs a warning when a removal fails. The cleanup also runs for failures that don't throw, e.g. an invalid `-addresstype`.
Commit 3 adds a release note.

How to reproduce:
```
cmake -B build -DBUILD_GUI=ON && cmake --build build
build/bin/bitcoin-qt -regtest -datadir=$(mktemp -d) -signer="python3 test/functional/mocks/invalid_signer.py"
```

Then click File, Create Wallet, Create. "External signer" is already ticked and the name is pre-filled as `trezor_t`.

On master: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'`, the process aborts, and `trezor_t/wallet.dat` is left behind.
With the PR: a "Create wallet failed" dialog appears, a retry shows the same dialog, and nothing is left on disk.

The tests `CreateWalletSignerFailure` and `CreateWalletInvalidArgs` in `wallet_tests` create wallets through the wallet loader, which is the same call the GUI makes. `wallet_signer.py` now expects -4, and checks that a failed creation leaves nothing behind, that a retry fails the same way, and that a directory, files or a dangling `wallet.dat` symlink that already existed are kept; in the symlink case the database created at the link's target stays too, and the check is skipped on Windows, as in `wallet_multiwallet.py`. An empty `wallet.dat` that already existed is initialized by the attempt and kept, so the name is taken afterwards, as before this PR.

You can see the tests fail without the fix:

```
git checkout HEAD~3 -- src/wallet/wallet.cpp
cmake --build build
build/bin/test_bitcoin --run_test=wallet_tests/CreateWalletSignerFailure,CreateWalletInvalidArgs
build/test/functional/wallet_signer.py
```
</description>

<commits>
491a7c9bd5 wallet: return an error when wallet setup throws

Setting up an external signer wallet throws std::runtime_error when the
signer fails, for example when it returns an invalid descriptor.
CreateWallet() didn't catch it. Over RPC this became a generic -1
error, but the GUI creates wallets on a worker thread with no handler,
so bitcoin-qt aborted.

Catch std::runtime_error around CWallet::CreateNew(), as
LoadWalletInternal() does when loading, and report it as a normal
creation failure. bitcoin-qt now shows its "Create wallet failed"
dialog, and createwallet returns RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4) instead of -1.

Update the affected wallet_signer.py error codes, and add a unit test
that creates the wallet through the wallet loader, as the GUI does.

5bce351252 wallet: remove the files of a failed creation

CreateWallet() creates the wallet directory and its database
(wallet.dat) before setting up the wallet. If setup then fails, they
are left behind and the name can't be used again: the next attempt
fails with "Database already exists". This happens for any setup
failure, over RPC as well as in the GUI.

Note what exists before the database is created. On failure, remove
the database files only if wallet.dat is new, and the directory only
if it is new and empty, as RestoreWallet() does. Check what exists
with fs::symlink_status(), as MakeDatabase() does, so that a
wallet.dat symlink counts as existing even if its target doesn't;
otherwise the cleanup would delete the user's link and leave the
database at its target. A path that can't be checked also counts as
existing. Use the non-throwing overloads, as the GUI does not catch
exceptions here, and log a warning when a removal fails.

Extend the unit test to retry the same name, add one for a failure
that doesn't throw, and check in wallet_signer.py that a directory and
files that already existed are kept. An empty wallet.dat that existed
before is initialized by the attempt and kept, so the name is taken
afterwards, as before this change; a dangling wallet.dat symlink is
kept together with the database created at its target. The symlink
case is skipped on Windows, as in wallet_multiwallet.py.

edc911450f doc: add release note for #36767
</commits>

diff --git a/doc/release-notes-36767.md b/doc/release-notes-36767.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..59d57aed45
--- /dev/null
+++ b/doc/release-notes-36767.md
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+Wallet
+------
+
+- `createwallet` now returns `RPC_WALLET_ERROR` (-4), with a message starting
+  with "Wallet creation failed.", when an external signer fails, is not
+  configured or more than one is found while the new wallet is being set up,
+  for example when the signer returns an invalid descriptor. Such failures
+  previously returned `RPC_MISC_ERROR` (-1) and made `bitcoin-qt` abort.
+- When creating a wallet fails, the directory and `wallet.dat` that the
+  attempt created are now removed, so that the name can be used again. Files
+  that existed before the attempt are kept. Files left behind by earlier
+  versions still have to be removed by hand.
diff --git a/src/wallet/test/wallet_tests.cpp b/src/wallet/test/wallet_tests.cpp
index de54302ef6..89dd2eadf0 100644
--- a/src/wallet/test/wallet_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/wallet/test/wallet_tests.cpp
@@ -34,6 +34,8 @@
 #include <test/util/setup_common.h>
 #include <test/util/time.h>
 #include <util/check.h>
+#include <util/fs.h>
+#include <util/result.h>
 #include <util/strencodings.h>
 #include <util/translation.h>
 #include <validation.h>
@@ -45,6 +47,7 @@
 #include <wallet/spend.h>
 #include <wallet/test/util.h>
 #include <wallet/test/wallet_test_fixture.h>
+#include <wallet/walletutil.h>
 
 #include <boost/test/unit_test.hpp>
 
@@ -795,6 +798,37 @@ BOOST_FIXTURE_TEST_CASE(CreateWalletWithoutChain, BasicTestingSetup)
     WaitForDeleteWallet(std::move(wallet));
 }
 
+BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(CreateWalletSignerFailure)
+{
+    // Without -signer, setting up an external signer wallet throws. Creating the
+    // wallet through the wallet loader, as the GUI does, must return the error
+    // instead of letting the exception escape.
+    const uint64_t flags{WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS | WALLET_FLAG_DISABLE_PRIVATE_KEYS | WALLET_FLAG_EXTERNAL_SIGNER};
+    std::vector<bilingual_str> warnings;
+    const auto wallet{m_wallet_loader->createWallet("signer_wallet", /*passphrase=*/{}, flags, warnings)};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(!wallet);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(util::ErrorString(wallet).original, "Wallet creation failed. restart bitcoind with -signer=<cmd>");
+    BOOST_CHECK(!fs::exists(GetWalletDir() / "signer_wallet"));
+
+    // Nothing was left behind, so creating a wallet with the same name fails for the same reason.
+    const auto retry{m_wallet_loader->createWallet("signer_wallet", /*passphrase=*/{}, flags, warnings)};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(!retry);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(util::ErrorString(retry).original, "Wallet creation failed. restart bitcoind with -signer=<cmd>");
+    BOOST_CHECK(!fs::exists(GetWalletDir() / "signer_wallet"));
+}
+
+BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(CreateWalletInvalidArgs)
+{
+    // Wallet creation can also fail without an exception, here because of an
+    // invalid -addresstype. The files created for the wallet are removed as well.
+    m_node.args->ForceSetArg("-addresstype", "invalid");
+    std::vector<bilingual_str> warnings;
+    const auto wallet{m_wallet_loader->createWallet("invalid_args", /*passphrase=*/{}, WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS, warnings)};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(!wallet);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(util::ErrorString(wallet).original, "Wallet creation failed. Unknown address type 'invalid'");
+    BOOST_CHECK(!fs::exists(GetWalletDir() / "invalid_args"));
+}
+
 BOOST_FIXTURE_TEST_CASE(RemoveTxs, TestChain100Setup)
 {
     m_args.ForceSetArg("-unsafesqlitesync", "1");
diff --git a/src/wallet/wallet.cpp b/src/wallet/wallet.cpp
index d6cc7ff728..10e2549c86 100644
--- a/src/wallet/wallet.cpp
+++ b/src/wallet/wallet.cpp
@@ -81,6 +81,7 @@
 #include <limits>
 #include <optional>
 #include <stdexcept>
+#include <system_error>
 #include <thread>
 #include <tuple>
 #include <utility>
@@ -363,6 +364,19 @@ std::shared_ptr<CWallet> CreateWallet(WalletContext& context, const std::string&
         return nullptr;
     }
 
+    // Note what exists before the database is created, so that a failed
+    // creation below only removes what was created here. As in MakeDatabase(),
+    // a symlink counts as existing even if its target does not. A path that
+    // cannot be checked also counts as existing, so that nothing is removed in
+    // doubt.
+    const auto not_found{[](const fs::path& path) {
+        std::error_code ec;
+        return fs::symlink_status(path, ec).type() == fs::file_type::not_found;
+    }};
+    const util::Result<fs::path> wallet_path{GetWalletPath(name)};
+    const bool created_wallet_dir{wallet_path && not_found(*wallet_path)};
+    const bool created_wallet_file{wallet_path && not_found(SQLiteDataFile(*wallet_path))};
+
     // Wallet::Verify will check if we're trying to create a wallet with a duplicate name.
     std::unique_ptr<WalletDatabase> database = MakeWalletDatabase(name, options, status, error);
     if (!database) {
@@ -370,11 +384,34 @@ std::shared_ptr<CWallet> CreateWallet(WalletContext& context, const std::string&
         status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_VERIFY;
         return nullptr;
     }
+    const std::vector<fs::path> database_files{database->Files()};
 
     // Make the wallet
     context.chain->initMessage(_("Creating wallet…"));
-    std::shared_ptr<CWallet> wallet = CWallet::CreateNew(context, name, std::move(database), wallet_creation_flags, born_encrypted, error, warnings);
+    std::shared_ptr<CWallet> wallet;
+    try {
+        wallet = CWallet::CreateNew(context, name, std::move(database), wallet_creation_flags, born_encrypted, error, warnings);
+    } catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
+        // Setting up the wallet can throw, for example when an external signer
+        // fails or returns an invalid descriptor.
+        error = Untranslated(e.what());
+    }
     if (!wallet) {
+        // Remove the files that were created for the wallet, so that the wallet
+        // name can be used again. Use non-throwing overloads, as the GUI does not
+        // catch exceptions here.
+        std::error_code ec;
+        if (created_wallet_file) {
+            for (const fs::path& file : database_files) {
+                fs::remove(file, ec);
+                if (ec) LogWarning("Failed to remove %s after wallet creation failed: %s", fs::PathToString(file), ec.message());
+            }
+        }
+        // This only removes the directory if it is empty.
+        if (created_wallet_dir) {
+            fs::remove(*wallet_path, ec);
+            if (ec) LogWarning("Failed to remove %s after wallet creation failed: %s", fs::PathToString(*wallet_path), ec.message());
+        }
         error = Untranslated("Wallet creation failed.") + Untranslated(" ") + error;
         status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_CREATE;
         return nullptr;
diff --git a/test/functional/wallet_signer.py b/test/functional/wallet_signer.py
index 20a5a3f3fc..0df9f86195 100755
--- a/test/functional/wallet_signer.py
+++ b/test/functional/wallet_signer.py
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@ Verify that a bitcoind node can use an external signer command
 See also rpc_signer.py for tests without wallet context.
 """

+import platform

 from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
@@ -81,7 +82,7 @@ class WalletSignerTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
 
 
         self.set_mock_result(self.nodes[1], '0 {"invalid json"}')
-        assert_raises_rpc_error(-1, 'Unable to parse JSON',
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, 'Unable to parse JSON',
             self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww2', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True
         )
         self.clear_mock_result(self.nodes[1])
@@ -247,13 +248,49 @@ class WalletSignerTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
     def test_invalid_signer(self):
         self.log.debug(f"-signer={self.mock_invalid_signer_path()}")
         self.log.info('Test invalid external signer')
-        assert_raises_rpc_error(-1, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+
+        self.log.info('Test that failed wallet creation removes the files it created')
+        # The cached chain has no wallets directory, so wallets are created in the chain directory
+        wallet_dir = self.nodes[1].chain_path / 'hww_invalid'
+        assert not wallet_dir.exists()
+        assert 'hww_invalid' not in [w['name'] for w in self.nodes[1].listwalletdir()['wallets']]
+
+        self.log.info('Test that retrying with the same name fails for the same reason')
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+        assert not wallet_dir.exists()
+
+        self.log.info('Test that failed wallet creation keeps a directory that already existed')
+        wallet_dir.mkdir()
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+        assert_equal(list(wallet_dir.iterdir()), [])
+
+        self.log.info('Test that failed wallet creation keeps files that already existed')
+        (wallet_dir / 'not_a_wallet.txt').touch()
+        (wallet_dir / 'wallet.dat').touch()
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+        assert_equal(sorted(p.name for p in wallet_dir.iterdir()), ['not_a_wallet.txt', 'wallet.dat'])
+        # The empty wallet.dat was initialized as a database before the signer failed.
+        # It is kept, as it was not created here, so the name is now taken.
+        assert 'hww_invalid' in [w['name'] for w in self.nodes[1].listwalletdir()['wallets']]
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Database already exists", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+
+        # Skipped on Windows, where symlinks behave non-standardly in cross-built binaries (see wallet_multiwallet.py)
+        if platform.system() != 'Windows':
+            self.log.info('Test that failed wallet creation keeps a wallet.dat symlink whose target does not exist')
+            (wallet_dir / 'not_a_wallet.txt').unlink()
+            (wallet_dir / 'wallet.dat').unlink()
+            (wallet_dir / 'wallet.dat').symlink_to(wallet_dir / 'target.dat')
+            assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "Invalid descriptor", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='hww_invalid', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+            # The symlink existed before, so nothing is removed: the link stays, and so does the database created at its target.
+            assert (wallet_dir / 'wallet.dat').is_symlink()
+            assert_equal(sorted(p.name for p in wallet_dir.iterdir()), ['target.dat', 'wallet.dat'])
 
     def test_multiple_signers(self):
         self.log.debug(f"-signer={self.mock_multi_signers_path()}")
         self.log.info('Test multiple external signers')
 
-        assert_raises_rpc_error(-1, "More than one external signer found", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='multi_hww', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-4, "More than one external signer found", self.nodes[1].createwallet, wallet_name='multi_hww', disable_private_keys=True, external_signer=True)
 
 if __name__ == '__main__':
     WalletSignerTest(__file__).main()
